Green lot · What goes to the roaster

Green lots

The green coffee itself: how much, what it cost, how dry, where it is kept, and what is left as roasts and sales draw on it.

Make the lot

What it is

A green lot is what goes to the roaster. Your own coffee points back to its run, and through it to the harvests and plots. Bought coffee keeps its origin as the seller states it. Every roast later picks a green lot as its source, and the stock goes down by itself.

Also inOne coffee, one chainKilos carry forward

Step 1 · Make a green lot from my run

Open Origin, the Green tab, and tap + Green lot. The Green lot code is made from the date (G, then year, month and day). Give it a Name people will recognise.

Try it in the app ›

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Step 2

Under From process, pick the run. Its chain shows, and a message: Green weight filled from the run, with the kilos from the run's last Out kg. Change it if the scale says otherwise.

Also inOne coffee, one chainKilos carry forward

Step 3 · Record the weight and what it cost

Under This lot, check the Green weight (required). Type the Cost of this lot: what you paid, or what it cost to grow and process. The cost per green kilo shows, and about what a roasted kilo costs at 15% weight loss. Add Bags and Bag size if it is bagged.

Try it in the app ›

Also inKilos carry forward

Step 4 · Note moisture and grade

Under Quality, type the Moisture %. With no water activity meter, the app estimates it from moisture (10 to 13% only) and says whether it is good for storage. For robusta it adds that the estimate is rough, because it is worked out from arabica figures. Add Density g/L, Screen size, Grade, Cup score and where it is kept under Storage.

Also inQuality as you goGuidance, not guarantee

Step 5

Tap Save. The lot's page shows its chain back to plot, harvest and run, how much is left, and This lot, Quality and stock, EUDR, Sack labels and For a buyer.

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Step 6 · Record coffee I bought in

For bought coffee, leave From process empty and fill Bought coffee: origin as the seller states it. The boxes are Farm or washing station, Producer, Region, Country, Variety, Process, Altitude, m, Harvest, Bought from, Lot or auction number, Invoice date. Use the words on the seller's papers.

Try it in the app ›

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Watch out

A lot with no process and nothing under Bought from still saves, with a message: Not linked to a process. Pick its process, or fill Bought from to mark it bought in. Without one of the two, nobody can tell where it came from.

Also inOne coffee, one chainRecords you can trust

Watch out

A green weight above what the run gave out saves too, with Green weight … kg is more than the process gave out. Your number is kept. Check the scale, or the run's last step.

Also inKilos carry forwardRecords you can trust

Keep the stock right

Step 7 · See how much is left

Tap Quality and stock: the kilos left, how many full bags that makes, and where it is stored. Roasts take their kilos off by themselves.

Try it in the app ›

Also inKilos carry forward

Step 8 · Record a sample, sale, count or new moisture

For anything else, add a line. + Moisture is a new moisture reading (every reading is kept, so you can watch it in storage). + Count/move is for after counting or moving bags. + Adjust is for anything else. Fill it in, tap Add line, then Save at the bottom.

Also inKilos carry forwardQuality as you go

Watch out

New stock lines are kept when you tap Save at the bottom of the lot; the page reminds you: New lines are kept when you tap Save.

Also inNothing gets lost

Why it matters

Moisture and water activity decide how long green coffee keeps. The app's guide aims for 11 to 11.5% for long storage. Above about 11.7%, water activity usually passes 0.61. In a long Cafe Imports study, lots above 0.61 lost more cup score in transit. A reading every few weeks shows a drift while there is time to act.

Also inQuality as you goGuidance, not guarantee

Labels

Step 9 · Print sack labels

Tap Sack labels: one 100 by 50 mm label per bag, with a QR, the lot code, name and estate, process, moisture, date and Bag 1 of 1. Tap Print at the top. The QR opens this lot in the app; once the lot has a passport, it opens the passport, which anyone can check.

Try it in the app ›

Also inOne coffee, one chain

Tip

If the labels do not open, the phone may be blocking pop-ups for the app. Allow them and tap Sack labels again.
